initial.name: run_code
initial.description: Execute a TypeScript program against the available tools. Takes two required arguments: `code`, the program to execute, and `description`, a short summary of what the program does. Call tools as `await tools.name(args)` per the declarations in the system prompt. Curate the program output. Image-bearing subtool results are attached after the run. The program contains TypeScript REPL statements; only erasable syntax is accepted, with no enum or namespaces. Type annotations are advisory. Top-level declarations and await are supported; top-level return is not supported. Emit output with console.log(...) or a final lossless JSON expression. Only printed values and that final expression become program output. Variables, functions, and imported modules remain in memory for this Agent across calls. Use await import(...) for modules. Direct filesystem access follows this execution's sandbox policy; process.env starts empty. Changing the session sandbox mode clears retained variables. An approved sandbox escalation runs in a separate temporary environment: it cannot access retained variables, and its declarations are discarded afterward. Restart, Agent disposal, cancellation, timeout, output overflow, or process failure clears the environment. If a variable is undefined, recreate it and reacquire its resources. State is not restored from the conversation, and failed evaluations can leave earlier mutations in memory. Redeclaring an existing let, const, or class name fails; assign to a mutable binding or use a new name. Await all tool calls; background callbacks cannot call tools after their evaluation ends. Await child-process completion before ending an evaluation; raw subprocess output belongs to whichever evaluation is active when it arrives. Each program starts in the Session's current directory. Running programs keep their initial directory. A sandbox escalation approves this complete program for one execution only. Nested tools retain their own policies and approvals. Request wider access only after evidence of a denial. Earlier effects may already have completed: inspect them before explicitly retrying. Programs are never replayed automatically.

code.description: The TypeScript program to execute, following this tool's execution instructions.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this program does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "Count TODO markers across packages"; "Read failing test and its fixture"; "Rename config key in every cordis.yml".

timeoutMs.description: Positive elapsed-time budget in milliseconds, including nested tool and approval waits. Default 120000; capped at 600000. Zero does not disable the deadline.

sandbox_permissions.description: Wider sandbox mode for this complete program execution; requires justification and approval.

justification.description: Reason this complete program needs wider access, shown to the user for approval. Use the language of the user’s current request.
